leads.title: Human origins in Africa established from fossils
leads.where: Taung and Sterkfontein, South Africa; Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania
leads.why: The Taung child and the finds that followed in southern and eastern Africa showed that upright walking preceded large brains and that humanity's deep ancestry is African.
leads.verify: Date the Taung find and its 1925 description, its long rejection, the Sterkfontein adults (1936-47) and the Olduvai finds (1959-64). Record Darwin's 1871 prediction, and treat the genetic evidence for a recent African origin (1987) as a later record.
search: Dart 1925 Australopithecus africanus man-ape of South Africa Nature
Broom Sterkfontein 1947 Mrs Ples acceptance Australopithecus

leads.title: Chromosome theory of heredity and gene mapping in New York
leads.why: Locating genes on chromosomes in the fruit fly gave heredity a physical basis and gave genetics its experimental method, including linkage maps and mutation studies.
leads.verify: Date Sutton's and Boveri's proposals (1902-03), Morgan's sex-linked white-eye mutant (1910), Sturtevant's first map (1913) and the 1915 book. Decide whether Boveri's work in Wurzburg is a separate origin.
search: Morgan 1910 sex limited inheritance in Drosophila
Sturtevant 1913 linear arrangement of six sex-linked factors

leads.title: The genetic code deciphered
leads.where: Bethesda, Maryland; Cambridge, England; Madison, Wisconsin
leads.why: Reading which triplet codes for which amino acid, and finding the code nearly universal, made it possible to interpret any gene and to engineer proteins.
leads.verify: Date the poly-U experiment (May 1961), the triplet proof by Crick and Brenner (1961), messenger RNA (1961) and the completion of the code (1966), and credit Khorana's and Ochoa's laboratories.
search: Nirenberg Matthaei 1961 dependence of cell-free protein synthesis poly-U
Crick Barnett Brenner Watts-Tobin 1961 general nature of the genetic code

leads.title: Programmable genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9
leads.where: Berkeley, California; Umea, Sweden; Vilnius, Lithuania
leads.why: A bacterial defence turned into a general tool made editing genes cheap and routine in research, crop breeding and the first gene-editing therapies.
leads.verify: Date the 2012 papers (Jinek and others; Gasiunas and others) and the first editing of human cells (January 2013). Record what it built on: the CRISPR repeats (Osaka 1987), their role in immunity (2005-2007), and earlier zinc-finger and TALE nucleases. Choose the primary place from the evidence.
search: Jinek Chylinski Doudna Charpentier 2012 programmable dual-RNA-guided DNA endonuclease
Cong Zhang 2013 multiplex genome engineering Mali Church 2013

leads.title: Systematic zoology and botany in classical Greece
leads.why: Descriptions of some five hundred animals with dissections, and a matching inquiry into plants, set the questions and the vocabulary of biology in the Greek, Arabic and Latin worlds for two thousand years.
leads.verify: Date Aristotle's work on Lesbos and the History of Animals, and Theophrastus's Enquiry into Plants. Check earlier written lists of animals and plants in Mesopotamia and Egypt and say why they do or do not count.
search: Aristotle History of Animals Lesbos lagoon date Leroi
Mesopotamian lexical lists animals plants Urra hubullu

leads.title: Solstice-aligned monuments in Neolithic Europe
leads.why: Farming communities built enclosures and tombs that marked the solstices, the oldest secure evidence anywhere of the year being tracked against the horizon.
leads.verify: Give the dated evidence for each of Goseck (c. 4900 BCE), Newgrange (c. 3200 BCE) and Stonehenge, and say which alignment claims are accepted. Check the rival early claim for Nabta Playa in Egypt, which is disputed, before keeping first_known.

concepts.name: Chromosome theory of heredity
concepts.summary: Knowing that genes lie in a line on chromosomes and being able to map their positions.

concepts.name: The genetic code
concepts.summary: Knowing how the sequence of bases in DNA and RNA specifies the sequence of amino acids in a protein.

concepts.name: Human origins in Africa
concepts.summary: Knowing from fossils that the human lineage arose in Africa over millions of years.

concepts.name: Programmable genome editing
concepts.summary: Cutting and rewriting a chosen DNA sequence in a living cell by supplying a short guide molecule.

concepts.name: Keeping the seasons by the Sun and stars
concepts.summary: Fixing the turning points of the year by watching where the Sun rises and sets on the horizon or when particular stars first appear.

concepts.name: Systematic natural history
concepts.summary: Describing, comparing and classifying kinds of animals and plants from direct observation, as a body of recorded knowledge.
